intro.title: visibility and opacity
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with interactive elements to learn how to control element visibility. You will explore the core CSS properties 'visibility' and 'opacity', understanding how they differ in hiding and showing content. The main technologies involved are CSS selectors and property values to manipulate visual states. By the end, you'll be able to apply these properties to create smooth visual effects and manage element display effectively.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, controlling visibility and opacity is essential for creating polished, interactive user interfaces. Developers use these properties to build features like dropdown menus that fade in and out, modal dialogs that appear with subtle transparency, and loading states where content becomes semi-transparent during data fetching. These techniques are commonly seen in e-commerce filters, admin dashboards with collapsible panels, and form validation where error messages appear and disappear smoothly. Mastering visibility and opacity allows developers to create more engaging, professional-looking interfaces that guide user attention effectively.
